findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (66 ayes, 47 noes)
findings.note: Voted yes on second reading of the omnibus election bill. The bill lengthens the time to 12:00 P.M. on the fifth business day after an election for a voter without photo ID to bring ID for a provisional ballot, and for a mail ballot with a missing ID copy to be fixed. It also treats certain extended Class C drivers licenses as valid photo ID for voting through 2027, and changes the citizenship question at drivers license voter registration.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, motion M11 to concur in the Senate committee substitute (62 ayes, 47 noes)
findings.note: Voted yes to concur in the Senate version of the omnibus election bill with the photo ID and ID cure provisions described above. The bill page shows the Governor vetoed it on 08/17/2026.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, second reading (House 66-47)
findings.note: Tyson's own vote on the member votes page is Aye on House second reading of HB 958. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) adds G.S. 163-83, which says the county board shall process a voter registration application only if it affirmatively indicates the applicant is a US citizen, with a 30-day notice and a statement under penalty of perjury if the answer is blank. It also requires removal processes for voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database.
